newsitem.title: UK: Cinven buys Macarthy Group for 55.5 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Cinven buys Macarthy Group for 55.5 mln stg.

text.p: British fund management firm Cinven Ltd said on Sunday it had bought the Macarthy Group, a maker of injectable and special medicines with a management buyout in a deal valued at 55.5 million pounds ($88.1 million).
Cinven said in a statement that Macarthy's main trading subsidiary is Matindale Pharmaceuticals, which makes specialist generic pharmaceuticals.
Macarthy was previously part of Lloyds Chemists, which was bought by German pharmaceutical group Gehe in January after a long takeover battle.
Cinven said the sale was part of Gehe's strategy to divest itself of the manufacturing businesses of Lloyds Chemists.
Macarthy's other main businesses include narcotics and opthalmics.
The group's existing management team will remain in place, Cinven said.

"Acquisitions are...likely to form a key element of development and Cinven intends to provide further funds in support of this strategy when appropriate opportunities are found," Brian Linden, a director of Cinven who will also be a non-executive director of Macarthy, said in a statement.
Cinven bought the health activities of French conglomerate Generale des Eaux in a deal valued at 1.1 billion pounds in July. -- London Newsroom +44171 542 7717 ($ = 0.629 British Pounds)
